blocks.title: Operator precedence
blocks.text: Operator precedence decides the order in which operations in an expression are performed. In Python, as in mathematics, some operators have higher precedence and are done first.
For example, in 3 + 2 * 5 the multiplication is done first: 3 + 10 = 13. Using parentheses makes complex expressions clearer and makes sure the operations happen in the intended order (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Define operator precedence and give an example where it affects the result (short question 3).
blocks.explanation: It is the rule that sets which operation is done first. 2 + 3 * 4 gives 14 because * comes before +, while (2 + 3) * 4 gives 20.

blocks.prompt: Long question 1: evaluate the five expressions, for example (b) (25 + 3 * 4 ** 2 - 6) / (2 ** 3 + 1) - 7 and (d) 45 / (2 ** 2 + 3 * 4) + 8 * (7 - 3).

items: Precedence: () first, then **, then * / // %, then + -; 3 + 2 * 5 = 13; parentheses make the intent clear.
